content:
**Visual observations:**
- Sugarcane plant viewed from above at ground level
- Leaves are severely bleached/straw-tan colored — nearly all green has been lost
- The discoloration runs longitudinally along the leaf blades (stripe pattern visible)
- Multiple leaves affected across the whole plant
- Leaves appear dried/scalded rather than spotty or mottled
- Some darker streaks visible within the tan/bleached leaf tissue

**Reasoning through the classes:**
- **Brown_Spot**: Ruled out — no discrete circular/oval brown lesions
- **Grassy_Shoot**: Ruled out — this is not proliferating thin shoots; these are dying leaves
- **Leaf_Scald**: Strong match — caused by *Xanthomonas albilineans*, produces cream/white longitudinal stripes that progress to complete straw-colored bleaching of entire leaves; advanced cases look exactly like this
- **Pokkah_Boeng**: Ruled out — no twisting/distortion or chlorotic patches on young leaves
- **Sett_Rot**: Ruled out — that's a basal/underground rot disease
- **Streak_Mosaic / Mosaic Virus**: Ruled out — mosaic diseases show irregular green/yellow mottling, not uniform tan bleaching
- **Yellow_Leaf**: Ruled out — yellow leaf shows yellow midrib contrast, not full-blade tan bleaching
- **Yellow_Spot**: Ruled out — no discrete yellow spots visible

The longitudinal stripe pattern progressing to complete straw/tan bleaching of entire leaves across the whole plant is the hallmark of advanced **Leaf_Scald** disease.
